topic.angle: A bolt is hotter than the Sun's surface

body.question: Which is hotter: a bolt of lightning, or the surface of the Sun?
body.reveal: The air in a lightning channel heats to about 28,000 °C (50,000 °F). The Sun's surface is around 5,500 °C, so lightning is about five times hotter.

probes.question: True or false: a lightning bolt is hotter than the surface of the Sun.

sources.title: NOAA National Weather Service: Lightning facts

image_brief.show: A dramatic lightning strike over a landscape at night

claims.claim: Lightning heats the air to about 50,000 F
claims.quote: it can heat the air to 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit (about 5 times hotter than the surface of the sun).

claims.note: Source gives only F; 28,000 C verified by arithmetic: (50,000-32)*5/9 = 27,760 C, rounds to about 28,000.

claims.claim: Lightning is about five times hotter than Sun's surface
claims.quote: about 5 times hotter than the surface of the sun

claims.claim: Probe: lightning bolt hotter than Sun's surface
claims.quote: about 5 times hotter than the surface of the sun
